headline: Learned models predict variant effects, regulatory activity and peptide-TCR specificity
label: Machine Learning For Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Deep learning and language models now target variant pathogenicity, regulatory elements and TCR-peptide specificity across recent preprints and papers.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of molecular function from sequence, structure and immunopeptide-level data using learned models. Several items adapt pretrained models: GLM-Missense fine-tunes a genomic language model and shows low concordance with six established missense predictors while adding complementary nucleotide-context information, and a yeast display study integrates fine-tuned protein language models into peptide recognition profiles for TCRs, reporting outperformance of AlphaFold3 on TCR recognition prediction. Other items use structure or regulatory priors: G-SPRI applies alpha-shape protein graphs to missense pathogenicity and driver recovery, BRIDGE links RNA sequence-structure motifs with noncoding variants for genome-wide RBP binding, and enhancer deep learning models prioritize 63 candidate breast cancer drugs. ArChIPelago shows that classic ML over multiple PWMs improves TFBS prediction across 704 ChIP-seq datasets. The new element is combining learned predictors with orthogonal evidence rather than replacing it, though generalization beyond these reported benchmarks is not established by the items.
